text:
anya: Heads-up — saw a regression in the prod nightly traces for fused flash attention + KV cache. Perfetto capture attached: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234

mike: link looks like the long tail on kernel "fused_flash_attn_fwd" spikes at kvcache write bursts, right? quick screenshot shows 3x wall time for that kernel around 00:12:34.

anya: yep. spike correlates with KV write storms when many short sequences (seq=8-16) hit the backend concurrently. nvprof/NSYS confirms heavy SM __serialize stalls.

devraj: can you paste the nsys summary? interested in kernel throughput vs occupancy.

anya: pasted below — this was nsys run from the nightly with workload generator: 
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=nightly_kv_writes.nsys
# sample top counters
Kernel Name                     Calls   Total Time (ms)  Avg (ms)  SMs Active
fused_flash_attn_fwd             412     1280.34           3.11      0.62
kv_write_kernel                 1240     920.12            0.74      0.88
kv_read_kernel                  3200     730.45            0.23      0.91
```

mike: fused_flash_attn_fwd has lower SM active (0.62) — that smells like memory-bound or serialization from KV writes. Does nvprof show L2 or shared mem stalls?

anya: nvprof shows L2_store_stalled and shared_mem_bank_conflict counters high for fused kernel during the spike. Notably when batching heuristic collapses short seqs into a single fused launch.

devraj: remind me — kernel selector currently picks fused variant for batch_size >= 16 OR when avg_seq >= 32. If avg_seq is small but many concurrent requests cause effective microbatches, selector sometimes picks fused path anyway because of combined batcher behavior.

tia: that's the batching heuristic bug I've suspected. Bursty tiny seq traffic leads to microbatch coalescing that tricks selector to fused path, which expects larger seqs and behaves poorly with heavy KV writes.

mike: can we reproduce with the microbench script? I'll run a quick perfetto + nsys with a synthetic pattern: many concurrent seq=12 requests at 80 qps.

profiling-bot: started run -> perfetto://run/2304509900; nsys -> s3://redwood-prof/nightly/repro_2304509900.nsys

mike: early results look similar. Timeline shows alternating kv_write_kernel bursts interleaved with fused_flash_attn_fwd. The fused kernel runtime jumps when kv_write overlaps.

anya: hypothesis: fused_flash_attn_fwd allocates/flushes KV slots or does non-blocking writes to global mem that serialize due to bank conflicts when many small seqs map to same cache lines.

devraj: idea: add a short-circuit in kernel selector to prefer non-fused flash variant when recent kvcache write qps > threshold or when avg_seq < 20 and concurrent_writes > 32. Quick A/B should show if unfusing helps.

tia: agree. can we also enable a per-stream KV write batching window to deconflict stores? e.g., group writes by key-range then perform coalesced writes. Might reduce L2_store_stalled counters.

mike: I'll push a patch to selector: if (recent_kv_writes_ratio > 0.2 && avg_seq < 20) select fwd_flash_nonfused(); running it now on the repro harness.

profiling-bot: deploy started -> canary-1234; self-check: no OOMs.

mike: patched — new run shows fused kernel calls drop 60% and overall latency p95 improves ~18%. NVPROF counters: L2_store_stalled down 45%, shared_mem_bank_conflict down 20%.

anya: nice. can you paste the perfetto timeline diff? the hot tail on fused kernel is gone for the same window.

mike: diff: https://perfetto.dev/trace/diff/2304509900_v2 — big improvement.

devraj: next steps: 1) roll selector change to nightly (toggle flag), 2) add telemetry metric for kv_write_qps and fused_kernel_collision_rate, 3) longer run to ensure no regression on large-seq workloads.

tia: I'll own telemetry. sending PR for metric names + thresholds.

anya: also let's add a small NVTX range around KV writes in the runtime so perfetto makes the overlap visible + a flag to enable per-request write coalescing.

profiling-bot: task created: PERF-487 add telemetry + selector toggle. assignees: devraj,tia.

mike: final note — this isn't a flaw in flash algorithm itself, it's a runtime interaction (batcher + kvcache writes) causing pathological overlap. marking as high priority since production had customer impact.

anya: thanks all. I'll document the repro and the fix in the internal runbook (links in the ticket). :thumbsup:
